concepts.name: Sagarmala Programme: Objectives, Nodal Ministry and Institutional Framework
key_dimensions: Nodal ministry is Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (not Ministry of Transport — common trap)
Four pillars: Port Modernisation, Port-Led Industrialisation, Port Connectivity Enhancement, Coastal Community Development
National Sagarmala Apex Committee (NSAC) chaired by Cabinet Minister vs. National Sagarmala Development Company (NSDC) as SPV
Distinction from Bharatmala: Sagarmala is port/waterway-centric; Bharatmala is road-centric

concepts.name: Bharatmala Pariyojana: Phases, Nodal Agency and Funding Architecture
key_dimensions: Nodal ministry: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways; implementing agency: NHAI and NHIDCL
Phase I target: ~34,800 km of national highways including Economic Corridors, Inter Corridors, Ring Roads, expressways
Funding mix: Central Road Fund, market borrowings, PPP, Toll-Operate-Transfer (TOT) model
Bharatmala Phase I subsumed earlier schemes like NHIDP; Phase II status and scope — a common confusion area

concepts.name: Port-Led Industrialisation under Sagarmala: Coastal Economic Zones (CEZs)
key_dimensions: CEZs conceptualised as clusters around major ports to attract manufacturing — comparison with SEZs and their legal basis
Distinction: CEZs are not statutory bodies under a separate Act unlike SEZs (SEZ Act 2005); they are policy constructs
Link to Make in India and reducing logistics cost for export-oriented industries
Environmental concerns: coastal regulation, CRZ norms as a constraint on CEZ development

concepts.name: National Logistics Policy (NLP) 2022: Linkage with Sagarmala and Bharatmala
key_dimensions: NLP 2022 is an overarching umbrella; Sagarmala and Bharatmala are sectoral instruments under it
Target: reduce logistics cost from ~13–14% of GDP to sub-8% (single-digit) — UPSC frequently tests the current figure vs. target
PM GatiShakti National Master Plan as the digital backbone integrating NLP, Sagarmala, Bharatmala
Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP) and Ease of Logistics (ELOG) as digital enablers under NLP

concepts.name: PM GatiShakti National Master Plan: Integration with Sagarmala and Bharatmala
key_dimensions: Launched October 2021; nodal department: DPIIT under Ministry of Commerce — not Ministry of Transport (trap)
Seven engines of growth: Roads, Railways, Airports, Ports, Mass Transport, Waterways, Logistics Infrastructure
GIS-based digital platform integrating 16 ministries for multimodal connectivity planning
Relationship: GatiShakti provides the planning layer; Sagarmala/Bharatmala are execution layers — frequently confused

concepts.name: Coastal Shipping and Ro-Ro/Ro-Pax Services under Sagarmala
key_dimensions: Ro-Ro (Roll-on/Roll-off for vehicles) vs. Ro-Pax (vehicles + passengers) — distinction matters for Prelims
Ghogha-Hazira and Ghogha-Dahej Ro-Pax services as flagship examples in Gujarat
Cabotage law relaxation: 2018 relaxation allowed foreign-flag vessels in coastal trade for specific cargo — significance and criticism
Coastal shipping's modal share remains low (~6%) despite policy push — reason and comparison with global benchmarks

concepts.name: Inland Waterways Development: NW-1 to NW-111 and IWAI's Role
key_dimensions: Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) under Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways — not a separate ministry
National Waterways Act 2016 declared 111 NWs; previously only 5 existed — the jump in numbers is a Prelims trap
NW-1 (Ganga: Allahabad–Haldia) under JMVP (Jal Marg Vikas Project) with World Bank funding
Sagarmala's waterway component vs. IWAI's independent mandate — overlap and coordination issues

concepts.name: Economic Corridors under Bharatmala: Classification and Strategic Importance
key_dimensions: Economic Corridors connect high-traffic production/consumption centres — distinct from inter corridors (connecting Economic Corridors to NHs) and ring roads
Key examples: Delhi-Mumbai Expressway (part of EC), Chennai-Bengaluru Expressway
Bharatmala focuses on improving average speed on NHs (target ~50 km/h from ~40 km/h) — a data point tested in Mains
Overlap with DMIC (Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor) alignment — spatial convergence but different nodal agencies

concepts.name: Toll-Operate-Transfer (TOT) Model in Bharatmala
key_dimensions: TOT: government monetises already-built NH assets by leasing toll rights to private players for a concession period — distinct from BOT (Build-Operate-Transfer)
Revenue to government is upfront lump sum; risk transfer to concessionaire for traffic shortfall
NHAI as the entity that bundles NH stretches into TOT bundles; first TOT bundle awarded 2018
Comparison with InvIT (Infrastructure Investment Trust) model — another NHAI monetisation route; both can appear in the same question

concepts.name: Multimodal Logistics Parks (MMLPs) under Bharatmala Phase I
key_dimensions: 35 MMLPs planned under Bharatmala as freight aggregation nodes combining road, rail, warehousing
Nodal agency: NHIDCL and NHAI in coordination with Ministry of Railways for last-mile rail connectivity
Distinction from Freight Villages (European concept) and Dry Ports — Prelims trap on terminology
MMLPs vs. Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC) terminals — DFC is Railways' domain; MMLPs are road-anchored multimodal hubs

concepts.name: Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFC): Linkage with Sagarmala and Bharatmala
key_dimensions: Eastern DFC (Ludhiana–Dankuni) and Western DFC (Dadri–JNPT) — JNPT linkage ties it to Sagarmala's port connectivity pillar
DFCCIL (Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Ltd.) is a separate SPV under Ministry of Railways — not under MoRTH
Speed advantage (avg freight train speed from 25 to 70 km/h) reduces logistics cost — directly linked to NLP target
Trap: DFC is not part of Bharatmala or Sagarmala organisationally, but convergence exists in planning under GatiShakti

concepts.name: Major Ports vs. Non-Major Ports: Governance, Capacity and Sagarmala's Scope
key_dimensions: 12 Major Ports (now under Major Ports Authority Act 2021, replacing MPT Act 1963) — governed by Centre
Non-Major/Minor Ports (~200+) — governed by respective State governments under Entry 31 of State List
Sagarmala targets both but capacity augmentation of Major Ports is primary focus — State coordination challenge
Major Ports Authority Act 2021 introduced Board of Port Authorities replacing Port Trust — governance reform angle

concepts.name: Coastal Community Development Pillar of Sagarmala: Fisher Folk and Skilling
key_dimensions: Fourth pillar often neglected in study — UPSC has set questions on the 'social' dimension of infrastructure projects
Focus on fishermen livelihood, skilling for port-related jobs, and development of coastal villages
Overlap with Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) — both target coastal communities but different nodal ministries
Criticism: displacement of fishing communities due to port expansion conflicts with this pillar — contradiction/paradox angle

concepts.name: NHIDCL vs. NHAI: Mandate, Jurisdiction and Relevance to Bharatmala
key_dimensions: NHAI: autonomous body under NHAI Act 1988 for national highways in general
NHIDCL: focuses on NHs in North-East and border states (strategic/defence connectivity) — a common Prelims confusion
Both implement Bharatmala but in different geographies — NHIDCL's North-East focus is the key differentiator
Border connectivity: NHIDCL roads link to BIMSTEC/SAARC corridors; strategic dimension tested in GS-2 and GS-3

concepts.name: Logistics Cost in India: Components, Benchmarks and Policy Targets
key_dimensions: India's logistics cost ~13–14% of GDP vs. USA ~8%, Germany ~6%, China ~10% — comparative data for Mains answers
High cost drivers: over-reliance on road transport (~60% freight by road vs. rail ~30%), poor warehousing, multiple check-points
NLP 2022 target: bring cost below 8% and improve ranking in Logistics Performance Index (LPI) — India ranked 38 in 2023 LPI (up from 44 in 2018)
Modal shift from road to rail/waterways as the structural solution — Sagarmala (waterways) and DFC (rail) are instruments

concepts.name: Sagarmala and the Blue Economy: Linkage and Distinction
key_dimensions: Blue Economy includes fisheries, offshore energy, marine tourism, seabed mining — broader than Sagarmala's port/shipping focus
Sagarmala is a subset of Blue Economy infrastructure; not synonymous — a conceptual trap in Mains
India's Draft Blue Economy Policy 2021 references Sagarmala for port connectivity but has separate pillars
EEZ management, deep-sea mining (Mission Deep Ocean) — adjacent concepts that appear in the same question as Sagarmala

concepts.name: Ring Roads, Bypass Roads and Congestion Relief under Bharatmala
key_dimensions: Ring roads around major cities (Delhi, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad) to divert through-traffic — reduces urban congestion and logistics time
Delhi-Mumbai Expressway includes bypasses around 8 major cities — integration of urban planning with NH development
Land acquisition under NH(A) Act 1956 vs. RFCTLARR Act 2013 — Bharatmala projects face land acquisition delays; a governance challenge
Green highways policy: plantation along NH corridors — environmental dimension of Bharatmala

concepts.name: Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Models in Port and Road Infrastructure
key_dimensions: Port PPP models: BOT (Build-Operate-Transfer), BOOT, Landlord Port model — Major Ports Authority Act 2021 facilitates landlord model
Road PPP: BOT-Toll, BOT-Annuity, HAM (Hybrid Annuity Model) — HAM introduced to revive stalled projects by sharing risk
Hybrid Annuity Model: government pays 40% construction cost upfront; 60% as annuity over concession period — frequently tested
Viability Gap Funding (VGF) as a complement to PPP in economically unviable but socially necessary projects

concepts.name: Connectivity with Neighbouring Countries: Bharatmala's Border and International Highway Projects
key_dimensions: India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway, Kaladan Multimodal Transit Transport Project (links to Sittwe Port, Myanmar) — Act East linkage
NHIDCL's role in building roads to international border check posts — strategic and trade dimension
Sagarmala's port connectivity to SAARC/BIMSTEC ports: Colombo, Chittagong, Chabahar — geopolitical overlap
Chabahar Port (Iran): India-financed, bypasses Pakistan, connects to INSTC (International North-South Transport Corridor) — standalone concept but intersects with Sagarmala

concepts.name: Environmental and Social Concerns: CRZ, Forest Clearance and Displacement in Sagarmala/Bharatmala Projects
key_dimensions: CRZ Notification 2019 relaxed norms for port-based infrastructure — criticism from environmentalists vs. government's development rationale
Bharatmala projects require forest diversion under Forest Conservation Act 1980 — Stage I and Stage II clearances as bottlenecks
Tribal displacement: Schedule V areas, PESA Act compliance in highway projects through tribal belts — GS-2/GS-3 overlap
CAG reports on Sagarmala and Bharatmala highlighting cost overruns, delayed land acquisition, environmental violations — accountability angle
